titulo: Shot size, angle and distance: the grammar every generator understands
lead: Shot size and angle aren't aesthetics: they decide what the audience sees and how they feel about the character. And it's a vocabulary that Google's official video prompt guide lists with names and examples. You leave with your scene's shot ladder written in the terms the prompt uses.
objetivo: choose the shot size and angle based on the audience's emotion, and write the scene's shot ladder in the generator's terms.

aprende.t: Read the shot ladder, from the wide shot to the detail
Use angle to convey power, fragility or unease
Know what the lens does to space
Write each choice with the term the generator understands

hero_alt: A cinema camera and four lenses of different sizes lined up on a black cloth, with a blurred set in the background.

secoes.sub: From the widest to the tightest. Each step answers a question.

nos.detalhe: Establishing or extreme wide shot: place, mood and scale. In English, establishing shot or extreme wide shot. It opens the scene and sets the rules of the world.
Wide shot: the whole body inside the place. It shows isolation, danger or power through the relationship between the person and the space. In English, wide shot.
Medium wide shot, from the knee up: action and body language. In English, medium wide shot or cowboy shot.
Medium shot, from the waist up: conversation and neutral, realistic movement. In English, medium shot.
Close-up, the face: strong emotion, decision, fear, joy. The closer you get, the more the audience feels. In English, close-up; the middle ground is the medium close-up.
Detail shot: a hand, an object, a texture. It reveals the clue that changes the story. In English, extreme close-up or macro.

secoes.legenda: Decision rule: if the place or the action matters more, go wide; if the emotion matters more, go tight; if a detail changes the story, go to the detail.

secoes.sub: Three decisions per shot, always based on what the audience should feel.

passos.sub: wide asks where; close asks how
texto: A wide shot answers "where are we?". A close shot answers "how does this feel?". The detail shows what changes the story.
A path that works: open wide to show the world, move in to reveal the emotion, and end on a close-up or detail for impact.

exemplo.texto: Wide shot of the dark street with the bakery lit up; medium shot of Dona Lia at the counter; close-up of her face lit by the oven.

texto: Eye level is neutral. A high angle, looking down, makes the character small or vulnerable. A low angle, looking up, makes them powerful or imposing.
A top-down shot gives a map-like view; a worm's-eye view exaggerates height; a dutch angle (tilted camera) brings discomfort. Use the dutch angle rarely, or it loses its force.

passos.titulo: The warning from the official guide
passos.sub: not every angle comes out the same
texto: Google's video prompt guide (Veo and Gemini Omni Flash, page updated on 10/15/2026) lists these angles and warns: some advanced angles and lenses are not officially supported, and results vary.
In practice, a simple, well-justified angle comes out more stable than a rare one. If the rare one doesn't work, swap it for a simple one with the same intent.

A wide-angle lens opens the field and exaggerates perspective: the place looks bigger. A telephoto lens narrows the field and compresses space: the background looks glued on and the subject is isolated.
Shallow depth of field keeps only the subject sharp and blurs the rest. It is a quiet way to say where to look (lesson 5).

secoes.sub: The vocabulary in Portuguese with the term used in prompts, and the ladder template. Angles, movements and lenses checked against Google's official guide on 10/19/2026.

exercicios.titulo: Ladder · your scene in 5 to 8 shots
exercicios.texto: Write the ladder for your scene: on each line, the size, the angle, and what the audience sees and feels. Vary it: at least 4 sizes and 3 angles. Check it in the section above and download the escada.txt into the project folder.
exercicios.pronto: the page answers OK: [n] shots with varied size and angle for your text, and the escada.txt is in the project folder.

exercicios.titulo: Swap · the most important shot with another angle
exercicios.texto: Pick the shot that carries the emotion of the scene and imagine it from another angle. At the end of the escada.txt, write a line starting with Swap: with the new angle and what changes in the audience's feeling.
exercicios.pronto: the escada.txt has, after the shots, a line that starts with Troca: with an angle different from the original and the effect in one sentence.

secoes.sub: Four questions. The explanation shows up after each answer.

perguntas.p: The scene needs to show that Dona Lia is alone in a neighborhood that is still asleep. Which shot size?
opcoes: Wide or establishing shot, with the place and the scale.
Close-up on the face, so the audience sees the emotion.
Detail shot of the hands covered in flour.
perguntas.explica: Loneliness in space is shown through the relationship between the person and the place: a wide or establishing shot. The close-up shows emotion, but it hides the empty neighborhood that gives the scene its meaning.

perguntas.p: According to Google's official guide, what does the low-angle shot do to the character?
opcoes: Makes the character small and vulnerable.
Gives a neutral view, as if from a person's height.
Creates a map-like view, seen from above.
Makes the character look powerful or imposing.
perguntas.explica: A camera below the subject, looking up, gives power. Small and vulnerable is the high camera; neutral is eye level; map view is the overhead.

perguntas.p: What does the official guide warn about advanced angles and lenses?
opcoes: That they only work in vertical video, 9:16.
That they are not officially supported and the result varies.
That they always require a reference image.
That they only apply to scenes without dialogue.
perguntas.explica: The guide says that some advanced angles and lenses are not officially supported and that the result varies. That is why a simple, justified angle is the most stable bet.

perguntas.p: When is the detail shot (extreme close-up) the right choice?
opcoes: Always in the first shot of the scene, to grab attention.
When the scene needs to show where we are.
When a detail changes the course of the story.
When the character talks to another.
perguntas.explica: The detail reveals the clue: the hand on the doorknob, the bread crust crackling. To show the place, go wide; for conversation, the medium shot or the over-the-shoulder shot work better.

itens.texto: Wide shows where; tight shows how it feels; detail shows the clue.
High makes small, low makes grand, eye level is neutral. Dutch, rarely.
Write the choice with the term the generator understands: wide shot, close-up, low-angle shot.
